title: ZeGA: Zero-Gradient Gated Adaptation via Weight-Space Synapse Cartridges

headline_result.text: Closed-form appended MLP channels (no gradients, no LLM editor) raised SwedMaster-300 on Ministral-3-8B from 73.67% to 84.00% while leaving base weights byte-identical.
headline_result.quote: improves SwedMaster-300 from 73.67% to 84.00% (+10.33 pp, p = 1.64 × 10−6 ),

key_claims.claim: ZeGA builds appended MLP channels in closed form from forward-pass calibration activations, without gradient optimization, and leaves base weights untouched.
key_claims.quote: ZeGA synthesizes closed-form structural width expansions (M → M + Kℓ ) from forward- pass calibration activations and attaches them directly to native nn.Linear layers

key_claims.claim: The author frames the work as extending Weight-Space Programming from compact circuits and the Qwen loop-dampening experiment to reversible adaptation of foundation models.
key_claims.quote: Extending WSP from compact circuits and single-direction loop dampening (Sparks Experiment 8) to reversible, context-selective adaptation in foundation models requires addressing three concrete challenges

key_claims.claim: On CLIP-ViT-B/32 the 4-row quartet raised CompBind-240 Group Score from 0.83% to 25.83%, while a 1-row control stayed at the base level.
key_claims.quote: whereas a 1-row control stays at 0.83%/3.33%/0.00% Group (p = 1.00).

key_claims.claim: On the Swedish language model, general benchmarks were preserved and Math-20 stayed at 7/20 with identical greedy completions.
In SDXL, the patch-gated cartridge converted target vessels while a constant-gate control destroyed bystanders.
key_claims.quote: while preserving nearby bystanders (85.91% all-8, 83.90% n = 7, 81.21% n = 6 naturalness vs. 4.11%/4.70%/5.09% for a matched constant-gate control;

limitations_stated.text: SpatialRel-160 group score remains below the i.i.d. chance reference.
limitations_stated.quote: SpatialRel-160 Group Score (6.25% quartet, 1.25% pair; quartet I2T 65.0%∗ , p = 0.0014) remains below the 16.67% i.i.d. reference

limitations_stated.text: Vision evaluation uses synthetic rendered vocabularies, not natural open-vocabulary benchmarks.
limitations_stated.quote: evaluates synthetic 3D attribute/relation vocabular- ies (0% template overlap) rather than open-vocabulary natural benchmarks such as Winoground [26] or SugarCrepe [10].

limitations_stated.text: No comparison against trained diffusion adapters; audio, video and convolutional extensions are future work.
limitations_stated.quote: Audio, video, trained diffusion adapter comparisons, and Family III convolutions remain future work.

notes_for_review: Cites Sparks of WSP as its paradigm but the weights are computed by closed-form SVD/ridge/polarization formulas, not written by an LLM, so it is better seen as a non-LLM, mechanical counterpart to WSP. Evidence is single-run, uses mostly author-built suites (SwedMaster-300, CompBind-240) and partial test sets (first 1,000 ScaLA items), with no LoRA or fine-tuning baseline actually run. Controls (1-row, constant-gate) are ablations of the method itself. The SDXL scalar offset was tuned on one development scene, reported separately.
